welcome.connect.intro: Signing in to a hosting service such as GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps brings its pull requests and issues into Glowfly, lets you clone from your account and publishes new repositories there.
welcome.connect.later: You can also do this later in {page}.
welcome.git.intro: Glowfly runs the Git installed on this computer, so your Git settings, hooks and credentials apply.
welcome.identity.email.help: Use the address your hosting service knows, so it links your commits to you.
welcome.identity.email.label: Email
welcome.identity.email_blank: Enter the email address to put on your commits.
welcome.identity.email_no_at: An email address has an @ in it.
welcome.identity.email_space: An email address can't contain spaces.
welcome.identity.from_git: These come from your global Git config. You can change them here.
welcome.identity.intro: Every commit carries a name and an email address. Glowfly saves them in your global Git config, so every repository on this computer uses them.
welcome.identity.name.help: Shown as the author of every commit you make.
welcome.identity.name.label: Name
welcome.identity.name_blank: Enter the name to put on your commits.
welcome.identity.not_during_switch: A profile switch is writing your Git config. Try again when it ends.
welcome.identity.profile_note: The change also goes to the {profile} profile.
welcome.identity.read_error: Your Git settings could not be read: {error}
welcome.identity.unknown: Git doesn't know who you are yet.
